title: Homogeneous quotients of finite-type group schemes by closed subgroups
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j:L\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion]; no normality, smoothness or affineness is assumed. There exist a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ and a $k$-morphism $p:G\to X$ that is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective, and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For every $k$-scheme $T$, the map $p_T:G(T)\to X(T)$ satisfies
$$p_T(a)=p_T(b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^{-1}b\in j_T(L(T)).$$
Here $G(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_k(T,G)$ and similarly for $L$ and $X$. For every $x\in X(T)$ there is an fpqc covering $\{T_a\to T\}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that each restriction $x|_{T_a}$ belongs to the image of $p_{T_a}$.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and its following sentence, printed p.105; Definition 5.20, printed p.104 (coset fibres and local lifts); Proposition 5.25, printed p.105 (faithful flatness). Finite presentation: Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01TX, lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation, and the finite-presentation permanence lemma; finite type over a field is Noetherian. Test-scheme version is the affine-local form of Definition 5.20.

proof.text: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and regard schemes as algebraic spaces. The closed subscheme $L$ of $G$ is finite type: on each member of a finite affine cover of $G$, its coordinate ring is a quotient of a finitely generated $k$-algebra, and these closed inverse images form a finite affine cover of $L$. Since a field is Noetherian, locally finite type implies locally finite presentation by the cited lemma. Every $k$-algebra is flat over $k$: a vector-space basis identifies tensoring with it with a direct sum of copies of the original vector space, preserving exactness. Thus $L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Define the left $L$-action on $G$ by $l\cdot g=g j(l)^{-1}$. The identity and action laws follow from inversion reversing products; cancellation and monicity of $j$ give freeness on every test scheme.

source.place: B.37 setup; field-flatness and finite-type affine calculation

proof.text: Apply the free flat action quotient to obtain the algebraic space $F=G/L$ and a surjective flat locally finitely presented $q:G\to F$. Its kernel-pair isomorphism, with inversion of the $L$ coordinate, reads $G\times_k L\simeq G\times_F G$, $(g,l)\mapsto(g,g j(l))$. Left multiplication by any $h\in G(T)$ commutes with the right $L_T$-action. It therefore induces an automorphism of the orbit presheaf over $T$ and, by the universal property of sheafification, an automorphism of $F_T$. The same construction with the universal $h$ gives a left $G$-action on $F$, with $q(g)=g\cdot q(1)$; all group identities hold by their identities before sheafification.

source.place: B.37 quotient and left translations; Stacks Tag 06PH

proof.text: The pullback of $\Delta_{F/k}$ by $q\times q:G\times_kG\to F\times_k F$ is $G\times_FG\hookrightarrow G\times_kG$. By the kernel-pair formula this is the inverse image of $j:L\hookrightarrow G$ under $(a,b)\mapsto a^{-1}b$, hence a closed immersion (on affine tests it is a quotient by the extended ideal). The covering calculus makes $q\times q$ an fppf covering, so closed-immersion descent makes $\Delta_{F/k}$ closed. In particular its scheme tests are quasi-compact. Thus $F$ is separated over $k$ and satisfies the diagonal hypothesis of the dense-scheme-open lemma.

source.place: separatedness of G/L from the closed subgroup; Stacks Tag 0420

proof.text: Apply source descent to $G\xrightarrow q F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: both maps are representable by algebraic spaces, $q$ is surjective flat lfp, and the composite is locally finite type. Hence $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally finite type. The continuous surjection $|G|\to|F|$ makes $|F|$ quasi-compact, since $|G|$ is quasi-compact. As $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated, the qcqs permanence lemma applied to $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that this morphism is quasi-compact. It is therefore finite type. Closed diagonals are quasi-compact, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has quasi-compact absolute diagonal; the diagonal factorization through $F\times_kF$ shows that $F$ is quasi-separated absolutely. The same holds for $G$. The qcqs permanence lemma now implies that $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with its local finite presentation this gives finite presentation.

source.place: finiteness properties of the homogeneous quotient; Stacks Tags 06EW and 01TX

proof.text: For each finite intermediate field $K$ of a fixed algebraic closure of $k$, let $V[K]$ be the union of all open subspaces of $F_K$ represented by schemes. This union is itself represented by a scheme: its representable open subfunctors form a Zariski covering, so apply the existing representability criterion. The index family is a set of open subsets of $|F_K|$, in the fixed universe. Each such union is stable under every left translation by $G(K)$, since translation is an automorphism and sends a scheme open to a scheme open. For $K\subseteq K'$, $(V[K])_{K'}\subseteq V[K']$, since a base change of a scheme open is a scheme open. The sheaf property needed by the criterion holds because algebraic spaces are fpqc sheaves, hence Zariski sheaves.

source.place: B.37 Step 1: maximal schematic opens and translation invariance

proof.text: The dense-scheme-open lemma supplies a dense scheme open $V\subseteq F$. It is nonempty since $q(1)$ is a point of $F$. Surjectivity of $q$ makes $q^{-1}V$ a nonempty open of $G$. Choose a nonempty principal affine open inside it, lying in a finite-type affine chart of $G$, and then a maximal ideal of its nonzero coordinate ring. Its residue field is finite over $k$ by the closed-point field lemma. After embedding that finite extension in the fixed algebraic closure, obtain $k_1/k$ and $g_0\in G(k_1)$ with $q(g_0)\in V[k_1](k_1)$. For every finite $K/k_1$, this point remains in $V[K]$. For any $g\in G(K)$, left translation by $g g_0^{-1}$ sends $q(g_0)$ to $q(g)$, so $q(G(K))\subseteq V[K]$.

source.place: B.37 Step 1: replace generic quotient construction by Stacks dense schematic open

proof.text: Apply finite-extension open exhaustion to the fixed finite-type scheme $G_{k_1}$ and to $W[K]=q_K^{-1}(V[K])$ for all finite $K/k_1$ in the fixed algebraic closure. Step 5 gives compatibility under extension and Step 6 gives $G_K(K)\subseteq W[K]$. Thus $W[K]=G_K$ for some finite $K/k_1$. As $q_K$ is surjective by base change, $V[K]=F_K$. Consequently $F_K$ is represented by a scheme $Y$. By base-change stability of finite type and separatedness, $Y$ is separated and finite type over $K$.

source.place: B.36 and B.37 Step 1: representability after a finite extension

proof.text: The left $G_K$-action on $Y$ has the $K$-point $o=q_K(1)$ with orbit map $q_K$. Base change preserves that this map is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation. The conditional homogeneous-scheme affine-neighbourhood lemma therefore applies, so every finite subset of $Y$ lies in an affine open. Notice that a scheme $Y$ has already been obtained in Step 7; this use supplies the descent condition, not existence of the quotient.

source.place: B.37 Step 2: affine neighbourhoods on the existing quotient

proof.text: The identification $Y\simeq F_K$ gives a descent datum $D$ on $Y$ for $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the two pullbacks over $K\otimes_kK$ both identify with the pullback of $F$, and their comparison satisfies the cocycle by cancellation of these identifications. These are schemes, since they are base changes of $Y$. A finite basis of $K/k$ makes $s$ finite flat and of finite presentation; it is surjective. Step 8 and the invariant-affine-neighbourhood theorem therefore give a transport-invariant affine neighbourhood of every point of $Y$. The invariant-affine-descent-gluing theorem then gives a $k$-scheme $X$ and an identification $X_K\simeq Y$ inducing $D$.

source.place: B.37 Step 3 and B.26: effective finite-field descent

proof.text: For each $k$-scheme $T$, the finite faithfully flat map $T_K\to T$ is an fpqc cover. Apply fpqc sheaf descent to both $F$ and the scheme $X$, viewed as an algebraic space. Their sections over $T$ are the respective equalizers for $T_K$ and $T_K\times_TT_K$. The compatible identification $X_K\simeq F_K$ identifies these equalizers, naturally in $T$. Hence $X\simeq F$ as sheaves. Transport $q$ to $p:G\to X$. This identification carries the separated finite-type structure map of $F$ and all four established properties of $q$ (flat, surjective, locally finitely presented, qc and qs) to $X$ and $p$. Thus $X$ and $p$ have the claimed geometric properties.

source.place: B.37 Step 3: identify the descended scheme with the quotient sheaf

proof.text: Evaluate $G\times_k L\simeq G\times_XG$, $(g,l)\mapsto(g,g j(l))$, on an arbitrary $k$-scheme $T$. If $p_T(a)=p_T(b)$, the pair $(a,b)$ gives an $l\in L(T)$ with $b=a j_T(l)$, so $a^{-1}b\in j_T(L(T))$. Conversely this equality produces a point of the kernel pair and therefore $p_T(a)=p_T(b)$. This uses all test schemes, not only fields or geometric points.

source.place: Definition 5.20 and Proposition 5.24: coset fibres on all test schemes

proof.text: Given $x:T\to X$, set $T'=T\times_XG$. The projection $T'\to T$ is flat and surjective by the covering calculus, and quasi-compact by base-change stability of quasi-compactness. For each affine open $A\subseteq T$, its inverse image in $T'$ is quasi-compact and has a finite affine open cover; the images of those affines cover $A$. Thus the singleton $\{T'\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering in the specified definition. The other projection $T'\to G$ lifts $x|_{T'}$, which proves the local-lift clause, including arbitrary non-affine $T$.

source.place: Definition 5.20: fpqc local sections from the quotient map
